name: Rosengartenschlucht
kurzbeschreibung: The wild Rosengartenschlucht gorge in Imst enchants visitors with roaring waterfalls, wooden walkways, the Blue Grotto, and lush flora.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wildly romantic Rosengartenschlucht gorge ranks among the most valuable and impressive natural monuments in Tyrol. Carving its way directly from the historic town centre of Imst over a distance of nearly two kilometers, this deeply incised limestone canyon ascends through the dramatic geological terraces of the middle mountain plateaus to the hamlet of Hoch-Imst. Over millennia, the tempestuous Schinderbach torrent has carved an astonishing natural spectacle of thunderous cascades, swirling potholes, shaded rock galleries, and lush moss-clad cliffs. The gorge owes its poetic name not to roses, but to ancient local legends and the delicate pale-pink flowers that cling to sheltered rock crevices. Near the upper end lies the enigmatic 'Blue Grotto', an ancient mining gallery where Romans quarried silver and lead over 2,000 years ago.

Route & Requirements

The gorge walk begins right in the heart of Imst beside the historic St. John's Church. Spanning approximately 1.5 kilometers, the secured trail ascends 250 meters of elevation in roughly 1.5 hours of walking (graded moderate, T2). Hikers follow sturdy wooden walkways pinned directly into sheer rock walls, stone staircases, tunnels, and footbridges running alongside foaming torrents. At the top, the cavernous basin of the Blue Grotto opens up, its pool shimmering with an ethereal turquoise glow in the sunlight. Sturdy footwear with grippy soles is mandatory due to damp timber boards and wet rock steps. The trail features numerous steps and is impassable for strollers and wheelchairs; surefooted children aged five and older will find it an exhilarating adventure. Dogs are permitted on a short leash.

Visit & Arrival

Rosengartenschlucht is accessible free of charge from early May to late October (closed in winter for safety due to ice and rockfall risks). Train passengers arrive at Imst-Pitztal railway station and take local city bus line 1 or 2 to the Stadtplatz or Johanneskirche stop at the gorge entrance. Motorists travel via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Imst) or toll-free over the Fernpass (B179) to Imst, with free parking available at the Pfarrplatz or sports centre. From Hoch-Imst, a convenient hiking shuttle runs back down to the town.

Tips

Combine your hike with a chairlift ride on the Imster Bergbahnen up to the Untermarkter Alm, then take the thrilling Alpine Coaster Imst – the world's longest alpine coaster – back down to the valley. On warm summer days, the mist from the waterfalls provides wonderful natural cooling.
preis: Gorge trail free of charge (hiking shuttle return approx. €2 to €3)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from early May to late October during daylight hours (closed in winter)
